memory_candidates.content: AskUserQuestion is measured categorically withheld from every Agent-tool dispatch of a named subagent_type (plain or subagent_type: "fork"), independent of tools:/disallowedTools: configuration, "All tools" registration, or frontmatter omission -- confirmed across 5 live dispatch configurations. The working remediation pattern already proven in this codebase (skill-slide-planning/skill-slide-critic) is: run every AskUserQuestion call in the INVOKING SKILL's own execution (either before the Agent-tool dispatch, or after it returns and before the next dispatch), never inside the dispatched agent itself. context: fork is a context-loading optimization only and grants no tool access on its own -- the calls work because of WHERE they execute (the skill), not because of that frontmatter field. When fixing a skill/agent pair built the wrong way around (the whole interactive workflow delegated into the subagent, as skill-meta/meta-builder-agent was), relocate the interactive stages verbatim (cut-and-paste, diff-reconciled) into a new non-eager context file the skill reads and executes in its own pre-delegation stage, leaving the agent as the terminal non-interactive writer that consumes already-collected answers.

A newly-added agent-system/extensions/{ext}/scripts/tests/test-*.sh file must be individually registered in that extension's manifest.json provides.scripts array, or check-extension-docs.sh (part of verify-deploy.sh's gate set) FAILS with 'script file on disk NOT in provides.scripts' on the next deploy-headless.sh run. This is unlike context/ files, where manifest.json can declare a whole directory wholesale (e.g. provides.context listing "workflows" once covers every file under context/workflows/). Discovered by running the gate itself, not anticipated at plan time -- when a plan adds a new scripts/tests/ file, add the manifest.json registration as part of the same phase rather than treating it as a later gate-driven surprise.
